cards.title: Asian Development Bank approves $500m loan to support Pakistan’s federal pension reforms
cards.author: Khaleeq Kiani
cards.why: This is critical for understanding Pakistan's fiscal policy, debt sustainability, and institutional governance reforms required for economic stability.
cards.summary: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved a $500 million loan to assist Pakistan in reforming its civil pension system. The move aims to address fiscal pressures as pension costs have grown fivefold since 2016. It supports the implementation of a new defined contribution scheme for employees hired from July 2024 onwards.
key_facts: Federal pension spending now exceeds Rs1 trillion annually.
Pension costs have increased fivefold since the 2016 fiscal year.
The loan supports the transition to a defined contribution pension scheme.
Employees appointed from July 2024 are covered under the new pension rules.

vocab.meaning: Related to government revenue, taxes, and debt.
The ability to be maintained at a certain rate or level.
A type of retirement plan where the amount paid is fixed based on contributions rather than a set final benefit.

text: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Tuesday approved a $500 million results-based loan to help Pakistan reform its federal civil pension system, the Manila-based lending agency said in a statement .

The reforms will help contain rising pension-related fiscal pressures, strengthen pension system sustainability, and expand fiscal space for development and social spending, according to the statement.
It added that Pakistan’s federal pension spending has grown nearly fivefold since fiscal year 2016 and now exceeds Rs1 trillion a year.

“Its longstanding unfunded and noncontributory legacy defined benefit scheme is financed entirely through annual budget allocations, creating growing fiscal pressure as pension obligations increase over time,” the statement highlighted.

“Pakistan has taken important steps to strengthen its federal pension system, and this program will help sustain and institutionalise those reforms,” ADB Country Director for Pakistan Emma Fan was quoted as saying.
“ADB’s support will help achieve lasting results by strengthening institutions, improving transparency, and supporting a more sustainable pension system,” Fan added.

Furthermore, the financing will support the first phase of the government’s Pension Reform Implementation Plan, and the transition to the defined contribution pension scheme, in which federal civil employees appointed from July 2024 are required to participate, said the statement.

“ADB’s support will help improve pension management to reduce liabilities, boost financial transparency through digital systems, and enhance pension service delivery and financial literacy among beneficiaries,” it read.
In 2024, ADB’s senior economist Aiko Kikkawa had said the pension system in Pakistan suffered from low contribution rates, making it unsustainable in the long run.

An earlier report by the ADB highlighted Pakistan’s weak pension and insurance systems. Most government positions entail unfunded pensions, where pensions for current employees are financed through tax revenues, according to the report titled ‘Strengthening Pakistan’s Pension and Insurance Systems’.

In August, the government executed agreements with 16 pension fund managers to formally operationalise the Defined Contribution Pension Fund Scheme (DCPFS), launched a year ago for public sector employees as part of major pension reforms aimed at containing the snowballing pension burden on the budget.

cards.title: Local govt polls in Punjab to be held in two phases
cards.author: Iftikhar A. Khan
cards.why: Understanding the timeline and structure of local government elections is essential for analyzing democratic decentralization and governance in Pakistan's largest province.
cards.summary: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has announced that local government polls in Punjab will be held in two phases starting in February 2027. Each phase will cover 18 districts across the province. This follows a long period of administrative uncertainty regarding local body governance in Punjab.
key_facts: Local government elections are scheduled for February 2027.
The process will be conducted in two phases.
The previous local body elections in Punjab were held in 2015 under the 2013 Act.
The PTI government dissolved elected local bodies in April 2019.

vocab.meaning: Something required as a prior condition.
Transfer of authority from a central government to local levels.

text: ISLAMABAD: Local government polls in Punjab, which are scheduled for February 2027, will be held in two phases, it emerged on Tuesday.

In a letter to the Punjab chief secretary, the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) said it had accepted the proposal conveyed by the province’s Local Government and Community Development Department secretary, in his letter dated Nov 16.
According to the letter seen by Dawn , the commission also directed its office to proceed with the conduct of local government elections and ensure timely completion of all prerequisite activities.
Under the agreed plan, elections will be held in 18 districts in each phase.

The first phase will cover Chakwal and Talagang, Pakpattan, Sialkot, Okara, Rajanpur, Narowal, Chiniot, Khanewal, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Rawalpindi and Murree, Dera Ghazi Khan and Taunsa, Lahore, Bahawalpur, Lodhran, Sargodha, Hafizabad and Bhakkar.

The second phase will cover Sahiwal, Gujranwala and Wazirabad, Bahawalnagar, Attock, Khushab, Mandi Bahauddin, Vehari, Jhelum, Sheikhupura, Muzaffargarh and Kot Addu, Toba Tek Singh, Faisalabad, Multan, Mianwali, Layyah, Jhang, Gujrat and Rahim Yar Khan.
The ECP also forwarded copies of the letter to the provincial election commissioner and the secretary of the Punjab Local Government and Community Development Department.

The last local government elections in Punjab were held in 2015 under the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013 . Polling took place in phases between October and December 2015, and elected councils assumed office in 2017 after indirect elections for mayors and chairpersons. Since then, local body polls in Punjab have experienced repeated delays.

The PTI government had dissolved the elected local bodies in April 2019 before they completed their tenure. The move was later struck down by the Supreme Court, which restored them. They eventually completed their term on Dec 31, 2021.

Successive provincial governments repeatedly amended or replaced the Punjab Local Government Act. Each legislative change required the ECP to restart preparations, including delimitation and election planning. Changing laws and administrative delays by successive governments contributed significantly to the postponement of the local body elections.

Under Article 140A of the Constitution and the Elections Act, local government elections should be held within 120 days of the expiry of local bodies’ terms. Since the councils’ term ended in Dec 2021, elections were due by April 2022, but they have been repeatedly postponed.

The ECP had initially proposed holding elections in Punjab on Dec 14. However, the provincial government had instead proposed elections in phases in April 2027, citing smog, dense fog and adverse winter weather conditions expected during December and January.

The ECP had rejected the proposal and, earlier this month, decided to hold the first phase of polls in Punjab on Feb 7, 2027. The decision came following a hearing conducted by a four-member bench headed by Chief Election Commission Sikandar Sultan Raja.
During the hearing, an ECP member pointed out that the provincial government had previously proposed holding elections in April.

However, the provincial chief secretary responded that the government had reconsidered its position and had no objection to elections in January or February, although April would be more suitable because of longer daylight hours and school holidays.

cards.title: Vehicles without fitness, emission tests to be barred from Islamabad to curb smog
cards.author: Iftikhar A. Khan
cards.why: Environmental policy and air quality management are vital components of current affairs, specifically regarding urban governance and public health.
cards.summary: To combat smog and air pollution, the government has banned vehicles without fitness and emission certificates from entering Islamabad. Authorities will impose heavy fines, register cases, and potentially arrest violators. Data shows Islamabad's average air quality has improved slightly compared to the same period in 2025.
key_facts: The ban targets vehicles lacking valid fitness and emission testing.
The average Air Quality Index (AQI) for Islamabad was 148 in October 2026.
The average AQI for October 2025 was 169.
Violators face potential First Information Reports (FIRs) and heavy fines.
The policy targets smoke-emitting industrial units and brick kilns alongside road traffic.

vocab.meaning: Fog or haze intensified by smoke and other atmospheric pollutants.
The production and discharge of something, especially gas or radiation.

text: ISLAMABAD: The government on Tuesday decided to bar vehicles without fitness and emission testing from entering Islamabad, as part of measures to curb smog and air pollution in the capital.
The decision was taken at a meeting chaired by Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry to review steps for smog prevention and reduction of air pollution.
The meeting reviewed the current smog situation in Islamabad, the Air Quality Index (AQI) and ongoing measures to control air pollution.

Chaudhry directed all relevant departments to ensure coordinated and effective measures to control air pollution and prevent smog. He said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi was himself monitoring the entire process of anti-smog measures in Islamabad and their implementation.
He contended that Islamabad’s AQI in October and November this year had remained better than the same period last year.
According to data published by the Pakistan Environmental Protection Agency (Pak-EPA), the average AQI index for Islamabad was 148 this October , compared to an average of 169 in October 2025 .
During the meeting, it was decided that heavy fines would be imposed on those involved in open burning and other smog-causing activities.

Chaudhry warned of first information reports, arrests and heavy fines against violators of environmental laws. Strict action would also be taken against smoke-emitting brick kilns and industrial units, he added.
The minister stressed that public cooperation was crucial for smog control and improvement in air quality, and citizens would have to play a responsible role.

The additional deputy commissioner (ADC) (General), ADC (Revenue), the senior superintendent of police (Operations) and the chief traffic officer attended the meeting, alongside the Pak-EPA and excise directors and other relevant officials.

In the past few years, air pollution has become one of the most pressing public health and environmental crises facing Pakistan. Various cities deal with smog, attributed mainly to industrial emissions, vehicular pollution , stubble burning and air movement .

Last month, a two-day Pakistan National Clean Air Conference concluded with the adoption of the Islamabad Clean Air Compact, calling for coordinated federal and provincial action, stricter enforcement, regular emissions inventories and annual reviews to tackle air pollution.

The National Assembly Standing Committee on Climate Change and Environmental Coordination has recommended the introduction of a regular vehicle emission testing mechanism in Islamabad and called for updating the Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997, to bring it in line with current environmental challenges and international commitments.
Last year, Pak-EPA launched large-scale inspections of vehicles and industrial units, while demolishing non-compliant brick kilns as part of a multi-tier plan to curb escalating air pollution.
